corrections.why: 12.2 m (40 ft) is the first 1933 tower. The register and firelookout.com give 50 ft for the 1949 replacement that stood until 1968. Newspaper items quoted on the Oregon page say 63 and 65 ft, so the editor should check which figure to keep.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and firelookout.com give 1933. The Oregon page quotes a 1934 CCC project item and a 1936 letter that says the tower was built. The story keeps 1933 and reports the later items.
The register and firelookout.com say 50 ft. The 1948 and 1949 newspaper items say 63 and 65 ft. The story gives both and does not choose.
A 1948 Myrtle Point Herald item puts the new tower 8 miles southeast of Powers; a 1948 Coos Bay Times item says 8 miles southwest. The story leaves the direction out.

notes_for_editor: Sources disagree on the first tower (1933 vs a mid-1930s build) and on the 1949 replacement (50 ft vs 63-65 ft); both are reported. facts.height_m is 12.2 m, the 40-foot 1933 tower the story leads with; the correction proposes 15.2 m (50 ft), the 1949 replacement's height, and the editor should decide. No source describes the site today and access is unknown. The willhiteweb.com page is about a Johnson Mountain in Snohomish County, Washington, a different peak, and was not used. Searches found nothing about this lookout's present condition. The Oregon page is a compiled set of newspaper clips and letters, so the 1934 and 1936 items are secondary quotations.
